title: Killing a finitely generated ideal in IB through a smooth algebra (flat square-zero base)
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\Lambda$ a commutative $R$-algebra and $I\subset R$ an ideal. Assume (1) $I^2=0$, (2) $\Lambda/I\Lambda$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R/I$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-smooth-algebras], and (3) $R\to\Lambda$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let $B$ be a smooth $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], $\varphi:B\to\Lambda$ a homomorphism of $R$-algebras, and $J\subset B$ a finitely generated ideal with $J\subset IB$ ($IB$ the ideal of $B$ generated by the image of $I$) and $\varphi(J)=0$. Then there are a smooth $R$-algebra $B'$ and homomorphisms of $R$-algebras $\alpha:B\to B'$ and $\beta:B'\to\Lambda$ with $\alpha(J)=0$ and $\beta\circ\alpha=\varphi$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07CL (lemma-lift-twice, line 1308) and its proof (lines 1326-1371: induction on the number of generators of J, Algebra Lemma 00HK lemma-flat-eq (equational criterion of flatness), Lemma Tag 07CK lemma-lift-once, formal smoothness of B)

proof.text: (Principal case: setup.) First let $J=(h)$ be principal, so $h\in IB$ and $\varphi(h)=0$. Since $IB$ is the set of finite sums of products of images of elements of $I$ with elements of $B$, write $h=\sum_{i=1}^k\epsilon_ib_i$ with $\epsilon_i\in I$ and $b_i\in B$. As $\varphi$ is $R$-linear, $\sum_{i=1}^k\epsilon_i\varphi(b_i)=\varphi(h)=0$ is a relation in the $R$-module $\Lambda$. Since $R\to\Lambda$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], $\Lambda$ is a flat $R$-module and by the equational criterion [lem-weil-pbc-flat-equational-criterion] this relation is trivial: there are $m\ge0$, $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_m\in\Lambda$ and $a_{ij}\in R$ with $\varphi(b_i)=\sum_{j=1}^ma_{ij}\lambda_j$ for every $i$ and $\sum_{i=1}^k\epsilon_ia_{ij}=0$ for every $j$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CL (lemma-lift-twice, line 1308), lines 1338-1344 (Algebra Lemma 00HK lemma-flat-eq)

proof.text: (The algebra $C$ is finitely presented.) Let $C=B[x_1,\dots,x_m]/(b_i-\sum_ja_{ij}x_j)_{i=1,\dots,k}$, with $\iota:B\to C$ the canonical map, an $R$-algebra via $R\to B\to C$. $B$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra by clause (i) of [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. The polynomial ring $B[x_1,\dots,x_m]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] is a finitely presented $B$-algebra (presentation with $m$ variables and no relations, [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]); its quotient $C$ by the ideal generated by the $k$ elements $b_i-\sum_ja_{ij}x_j$ is a finitely presented $B$-algebra by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-quotient-fg-ideal]; hence $C$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra by part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition] applied to $R\to B\to C$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CL (lemma-lift-twice, line 1308), lines 1345-1349 (definition of C; its finite presentation over R, needed to apply Lemma 07CK, is left implicit in the source)

proof.text: (The map $C\to\Lambda$.) Regard $\Lambda$ as a $B$-algebra via $\varphi$. By the universal property of the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] there is a unique $B$-algebra map $B[x_1,\dots,x_m]\to\Lambda$ with $x_j\mapsto\lambda_j$; it sends $b_i-\sum_ja_{ij}x_j$ to $\varphi(b_i)-\sum_ja_{ij}\lambda_j=0$ (step 1), hence factors through a $B$-algebra (so $R$-algebra) map $\varphi_C:C\to\Lambda$, and $\varphi_C\circ\iota=\varphi$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CL (lemma-lift-twice, line 1308), lines 1349-1350 ('with C -> Lambda given by phi and x_j -> lambda_j')

proof.text: (Lift once.) By hypotheses (1) $I^2=0$ and (2), and since $C$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra (step 2), [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-lift-once] applied to $\varphi_C:C\to\Lambda$ gives a smooth $R$-algebra $B'$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], a finitely generated ideal $J'\subset B'$ with $J'\subset IB'$, and $R$-algebra maps $\psi:C\to B'/J'$, $\chi:B'/J'\to\Lambda$ with $\chi\circ\psi=\varphi_C$. Let $q:B'\to B'/J'$ be the quotient map and $\beta=\chi\circ q:B'\to\Lambda$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CL (lemma-lift-twice, line 1308), lines 1351-1355 (Lemma 07CK lemma-lift-once); beta is not named in the source: it is B' -> B'/J' -> Lambda

proof.text: (Lift through the square-zero ideal $J'$.) $(J')^2\subset(IB')^2=I^2B'=0$ by (1). Since $R\to B$ is smooth, [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-square-zero-lifting] applied with $D=B'$, $N=J'$ and the $R$-algebra map $g=\psi\circ\iota:B\to B'/J'$ gives an $R$-algebra map $\alpha:B\to B'$ with $q\circ\alpha=\psi\circ\iota$. Then $\beta\circ\alpha=\chi\circ q\circ\alpha=\chi\circ\psi\circ\iota=\varphi_C\circ\iota=\varphi$ (step 3).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CL (lemma-lift-twice, line 1308), lines 1355-1357 ('Since B is smooth over R we can lift the map B -> C -> B'/J' ... Then phi = beta o alpha'; formal smoothness, Algebra 00TN/00TI; that J' is square-zero is left implicit)

proof.text: ($\alpha$ kills $h$.) For each $j$ choose $\xi_j\in B'$ with $q(\xi_j)=\psi(\bar x_j)$, $\bar x_j$ the class of $x_j$ in $C$. In $C$ we have $\iota(b_i)=\sum_ja_{ij}\bar x_j$, so $q(\alpha(b_i))=\psi(\iota(b_i))=\sum_ja_{ij}\psi(\bar x_j)=q(\sum_ja_{ij}\xi_j)$ and $\theta_i:=\alpha(b_i)-\sum_ja_{ij}\xi_j\in J'\subset IB'$. As $\alpha$ is $R$-linear, $\alpha(h)=\sum_i\epsilon_i\alpha(b_i)=\sum_j\bigl(\sum_i\epsilon_ia_{ij}\bigr)\xi_j+\sum_i\epsilon_i\theta_i=0$: the first sum vanishes by step 1 and $\epsilon_i\theta_i\in I\cdot IB'=I^2B'=0$. Hence $\alpha(J)=\alpha(hB)=0$, and with steps 4-5 the lemma holds when $J$ is principal.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CL (lemma-lift-twice, line 1308), lines 1357-1370

proof.text: (Induction on the number of generators.) Claim $P(n)$: the lemma holds for every $B,\varphi$ and every $J$ generated by $n$ elements. $P(0)$: $J=0$; take $B'=B$, $\alpha=\mathrm{id}$, $\beta=\varphi$. $P(1)$ is steps 1-6. Assume $P(n-1)$ with $n\ge2$ and let $J=(h_1,\dots,h_n)\subset IB$ with $\varphi(J)=0$. Apply $P(1)$ to $(h_n)\subset IB$: there are a smooth $R$-algebra $B_1$ and $R$-algebra maps $\alpha_1:B\to B_1$, $\beta_1:B_1\to\Lambda$ with $\alpha_1(h_n)=0$ and $\beta_1\alpha_1=\varphi$. Let $J_1\subset B_1$ be the ideal generated by $\alpha_1(h_1),\dots,\alpha_1(h_{n-1})$; then $J_1\subset IB_1$ (as $\alpha_1(IB)\subset IB_1$) and $\beta_1(J_1)=0$ (as $\beta_1\alpha_1(h_l)=\varphi(h_l)=0$). $P(n-1)$ applied to $\beta_1,J_1$ gives a smooth $R$-algebra $B'$ and $\alpha_2:B_1\to B'$, $\beta:B'\to\Lambda$ with $\alpha_2(J_1)=0$ and $\beta\alpha_2=\beta_1$. Then $\alpha=\alpha_2\alpha_1$ kills $h_1,\dots,h_n$, so $\alpha(J)=0$, and $\beta\alpha=\beta_1\alpha_1=\varphi$. Since $J$ is finitely generated, $P(n)$ for its number of generators is the lemma.
